successors.name: Italia (Social War confederation)
successors.text: Samnium: the Pentri, Caraceni, Caudini and Hirpini

ledger.x: c. 500 BC: the Samnite confederation. 'An Oscan-speaking Italic people who inhabited Samnium, a region in the modern inland Abruzzo, Molise, and Campania', who 'formed a confederation consisting of four tribes' (Hirpini, Caudini, Caraceni, Pentri; 'Bovianum is the capital of the Pentri'). No page dates the…
341 BC: peace; Rome 'withdrew after the Latin revolt' (expansion page).
328 BC: 'Fregellae (328 BC): A Roman colony was founded there; the Samnites later took it' (and lost it again).
326-304 BC: the Second Samnite War ('327-304 BC' infobox; 'Fighting resumed in 326 BC').
314 BC: Luceria retaken by Rome after the Samnites 'seized it after its garrison betrayed Rome'.
304 BC: 'Rome annexed large Samnite territories and founded colonies there' (expansion page); 'Rome annexed Bovianum and Fregellae' (Samnites page); 'the ancient treaty was restored'.
304 BC: 'Peace of 304 BC: The ancient treaty was restored'.

298-290 BC: the Third Samnite War. the war broke out in 298 ('The latter was the year the Third Samnite War broke out'; the Samnite Wars page places Camerinum in the 310 Etruscan campaign, not here); Sentinum (295) lost with the Senones, Etruscans and Umbrians; Aquilonia; Venusia of the Hirpini 'seized in 291 BC'.
290 BC: 'In 290 BC the consuls mopped up remaining resistance'.

290 BC: 'the Samnites were subjugated in 290 BC'; 'Samnium was conquered and the Samnites were assimilated into Roman society'; they stay on their land as allies of Rome, tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start samnites 290).
91 BC: 'After Rome refused them citizenship, the Samnites rebelled' (Social War, 91-88); roman-republic /ledger/128 ends the tie in 91.

91 BC: Samnium joins the Italian confederation of the Social War (Cliopatria's Italian City-States); the Samnites are granted citizenship after the war and Sulla punishes them after the Colline Gate (82): 'some of their cities have now dwindled into villages'.

wars.name: First Samnite War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; peace after 'three Samnite defeats and a Roman invasion'

wars.name: Second Samnite War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; 'Rome annexed large Samnite territories'

wars.name: Third Samnite War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Sentinum (295), Aquilonia, Samnium 'subjugated in 290 BC'

certainty.note: Samnium and Campania have no surveyed borders; provinces and circles stand for them.
